    Strict hook and cohook morphisms #

    Every hook or cohook adds at least one word position. The canonical hook projection kills a new position, while the canonical cohook inclusion misses one. Thus the four right-module maps at the two word endpoints are proper epimorphisms or proper monomorphisms. String-module indecomposability then rules out a splitting in the other direction as well.

    source
    theorem MagnitudeConjecture.BoundQuiver.StringWord.Word.RightExtension.not_exists_position_targetPosition {k Q : Type u} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {R : RelationFamily k Q} {C D : Word R} (extension : C.RightExtension D) (hsteps : extension.steps ≠ 0) :
    ¬∃ (i : C.PositionAt D.target), extension.position i = D.targetPosition

    The final position of a nontrivial right extension is not inherited from the original word.

    source
    theorem MagnitudeConjecture.BoundQuiver.StringWord.Word.RightExtension.spaceInclusion_not_surjective {k Q : Type u} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {R : RelationFamily k Q} {C D : Word R} (extension : C.RightExtension D) (hsteps : extension.steps ≠ 0) :
    ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(extension.spaceInclusion D.target)

    The coordinate inclusion of a nontrivial right extension misses its new final position.
